Benchmark Report: TaktX BPMN Engine

TL;DR: Scalability at a fraction of the cost

What we measured:

TaktX sustained starting ~1,700 PI/s on a “typical” BPMN model (10×200 ms tasks + 2×1-min timers) using just 2×4-vCPU engine nodes and a small 3×2-vCPU broker cluster — with p95 < 500 ms and over 200k concurrent instances at any given time.

What it means:

That’s ~20–50× higher throughput per node than what teams commonly report for database-centric engines on similar “typical” models. Hitting the same load with TaktX usually means 70–90% fewer cores (and fewer machines), no scale-up RDBMS tier, and simpler ops. This also means that updates are broadcasted in near real-time resulting in very reactive frontend showing the actual process instance state near real time with 100-200ms latency during low loads and still sub-second latency during very high loads.

Savings:

  • Compute spend: Cut server counts dramatically to reach the same PI/s.
  • Platform spend: Eliminate relational DB clusters used as workflow backbones.
  • Energy & carbon: Fewer nodes → lower power, cooling, and footprint.
  • Predictable scaling: Add partitions or a small node to scale linearly, instead of costly DB upgrades.

Bottom line:

Same (or better) SLAs with far less hardware. TaktX drives the €/$ per process instance way down, making high-volume automation economically viable on modest infrastructure.
